findings.reason: the implementer must be told the rule keys on the remedy the refusal publishes (the review-command pattern first, `max` by length), not on whether the text contains any dispatch invocation, or the node builds a rule that fails its own second negative case.
findings.text: §2's rule says `_queued_failure_remedy` returns no remedy "for a refusal that quotes a `reckon crew dispatch` invocation among its remedies", but the plan-review gate's own refusal text quotes a dispatch invocation as well as the review command: `reckon/crew/refusals.py` D23 renders "Resolve with `reckon crew review` for the plan, ... then `reckon crew dispatch`; or `reckon crew dispatch --allow-unreviewed-plan` to waive the review". The section's done-when on line 38 requires that same `PlanReviewMissing` failure to still yield `queued-awaiting-session` with its `reckon crew review` command, and `_remedy_command_stated_by` only returns the review command because `_QUOTED_REVIEW_COMMAND` is tried before `_QUOTED_COMMAND` with `max(..., key=len)`. A literal implementation of the deliverable's wording therefore contradicts the deliverable's own test, and the two halves of the section disagree about which remedy the rule inspects

findings.reason: if the station replaces the producer before §3 lands on it the reap is written into a loop that is deleted, and if §3 lands first the station must be told to carry the call, so the plan needs the dependency declared in the direction it actually runs and §3 needs to name the station tick beside `watch_ticker`
findings.text: §3 adds its reap call to `recovery_watch.watch_ticker`, described as "the producer loop ... on each tick", but `docs/plans/the-monitor-reads-each-fact-once.html` §7 is titled "One station per node replaces the per-project producers" and is declared `implementable`, so the producer that §3 patches is the process another active plan retires; the plan records that relationship as `plan-informs: the-monitor-reads-each-fact-once`, which is the reciprocal of `depends-on` and therefore states that the station plan depends on this one, when the coupling runs the other way — this plan's §3 call site is owned by the station plan's outcome

findings.reason: the anchor resolves and the plan states the pids, timestamps and run id in its own prose, so the root cause does not rest on §10; the citation is a provenance pointer that a reader will find empty, not a claim the plan argues from.
findings.text: §1 offers `monitor-storage-load-rca §10` as the record in which both findings were made, but §10 ("A second reading on 2026-10-23: what still loads the node") contains neither: it holds no zombie, no pid (4098806, 1527007, 464271 all absent), no run id (`135622629487` absent) and no `UnreconciledRuns` refusal, and its own closing line says it "confirms §3's diagnosis and adds one cause §3 did not name: the workers themselves", naming only file-syscall readers

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — every file, symbol and href the plan cites resolves (`recovery_classification._queued_failure_remedy`, `queue_admission.admit_until_stopped`, `recovery_watch.watch_ticker`, `process_signal.py`, `dispatch_launch._export_launched_workers_for_reexec`, the `follower_reload` module, `/reckon/research/monitor-storage-load-rca#s10` with `.html` appended), but §1's citation of §10 does not carry the two findings it is offered as the record of.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — each section names a test file, a measurable outcome, and an explicit negative control (`§2` "without the dispatch-remedy rule, the first two cases report `queued-awaiting-session` and fail"; `§3` "a helper that records no children leaves the inherited child a zombie").
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the evidence the plan names is test files under `tests/` in the repository and code paths in `reckon/crew/`; no gate log, scratchpad or node-local path is named.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag appears as or inside a symbol, filename or comment; `reap_inherited_children` and both test filenames are named by mechanism.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §2's rule as written ("a refusal that quotes a `reckon crew dispatch` invocation among its remedies") strips the duty from the plan-review gate's refusal, which the same section's done-when requires to keep it.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §2 is one change to `_queued_failure_remedy`; §3 is one helper plus its three named call sites; §1 carries no deliverable (`done`), and the followup builds §2 and §3 together.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §3 patches `recovery_watch.watch_ticker`, the per-project producer loop that `the-monitor-reads-each-fact-once` §7 (status `implementable`) is planned to replace, and the plan declares that relationship only as `plan-informs`, in the direction that says the station plan depends on this one.
